name: WorkMeetingAccessibilityAuditFindings_no_va

custom.system_prompt: Team reviewing accessibility audit findings and prioritizing fixes under time pressure. Kenji (design), Zara (eng), Amara (PM), Noor (accessibility specialist). Noor's findings are more severe than expected.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Small office, video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate a meeting reviewing results from an external accessibility audit. Noor presents findings, several more severe than the team expected, including some legal compliance risk. Kenji and Zara discuss what's fixable quickly versus what needs real design rework. Amara has to prioritize against existing roadmap commitments. They land on a phased remediation plan.

variations.context: Meeting reviewing external accessibility audit findings and planning remediation

setting.mood: Sobering at first — the findings are worse than expected — settling into practical planning.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Cross-functional colleagues taking this seriously, not defensively.
setting.background: The audit was done by an external firm ahead of a compliance deadline.
setting.conversation_style: Serious and specific — real findings, real severity levels, real deadlines.

scenario_template.topic: Noor presents the audit findings, several more severe than expected, including compliance risk.
scenario_template.note: Specific severity levels, not vague concern. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Kenji and Zara triage what's a quick fix versus what needs real design rework.
scenario_template.note: Honest about the harder items, not minimizing. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Amara weighs this against existing roadmap commitments given the compliance deadline.
scenario_template.note: Something on the roadmap has to move. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: They agree on a phased remediation plan with clear ownership and dates.
scenario_template.note: Specific, dated commitments. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
